note_on_method: Portland gets three filter pages of the five, and it is the first city in this directory to earn either the indoor one or the free one. That is because Portland is the first operator to write either fact down. The lights page does not exist here: Portland Parks & Recreation says nothing about lighting at any of its eleven venues, and an unchecked light is not an unlit one.

slots.why_this_filter: Outdoor is the default in most of this directory and a live decision in Portland. Seven of the eleven venues have outdoor courts and they hold 45 of the city's 59, but they are open dawn to dusk in a city where dusk is half past four in December, on surfaces the parks department warns are slippery when wet. Six of the seven are free, which only a handful of other cities in this directory can say of a single venue. The seventh, Portland Tennis Center, has sixteen courts, and its pickleball runs only from mid June to early September. So this page is really two lists: 29 courts you can walk onto for nothing on any dry morning, and 16 more that exist for one summer programme.
slots.what_qualifies: A venue appears here when a source places its courts outdoors. For all seven, Portland Parks & Recreation lists them under a heading reading "Outdoor courts" (or, for the tennis centre, describes "16 outdoor hard courts") and uses the word outdoor in the venue's own line. Nothing is inferred from a park being a park. The four community centres are absent because their courts are indoor.

faqs.q: How many outdoor pickleball courts does Portland have?
faqs.a: Forty-five across seven venues. Twenty-nine are the free park courts: eight each at Columbia and Sellwood, six at Gabriel, four at Pier, two at Laurelhurst and one at Hillside. The other sixteen are at the Portland Tennis Center and are available for pickleball only through a summer programme.

faqs.q: Are the outdoor courts open all year?
faqs.a: The six park sites are, dawn to dusk, first-come and first-served, with the city asking players to limit a session to an hour when others are waiting. No winter closure is published. What changes is daylight and weather: the city's rules include the line that the surface is slippery when wet. The Portland Tennis Center is the exception: its pickleball runs mid June to early September.

faqs.q: Do the outdoor courts have lights?
faqs.a: Unknown, at any of them. Portland Parks & Recreation does not mention lighting for a single one of its eleven pickleball venues, so every venue reads "not stated" for lights rather than "no". That is also why Portland has no lights page.

faqs.q: Which outdoor site should I pick?
faqs.a: For volume, Columbia Park or Sellwood Park, eight courts each and free, at opposite ends of the city. For turning up with nothing but a paddle, Gabriel Park, whose six dedicated courts include nets. For a short game near the inner east side, Laurelhurst's two. Hillside's single court is for people who live near it. The Portland Tennis Center's sixteen are available for pickleball only between mid June and early September.

slots.why_this_filter: This is the first indoor page in the directory, and Portland is the right city to have earned it. Between October and May the free outdoor courts are a few hours of grey daylight on a wet hard surface, and the fourteen indoor courts across four community centres are the difference between playing and not. They are also the only pickleball in the city with a published price: $6 for adults and $5 for seniors per drop-in session, which is the first cost figure any operator in this directory has stated. Five courts at Southwest, four at East Portland, three at Montavilla, two at St. Johns.
slots.what_qualifies: A venue is here only if a source states that it has indoor courts. All four are listed by Portland Parks & Recreation under a heading reading "Indoor Courts" with a court count on the same line. Covered courts do not qualify and climate control does not qualify: a roof over an outdoor court is not an indoor court. No Portland venue was excluded on those grounds, because the city describes no covered courts at all.

faqs.q: How much does indoor pickleball cost in Portland?
faqs.a: $6 for adults and $5 for seniors per drop-in session at all four community centres. That is the city's own published figure and it was the first price any operator in this directory stated. It covers drop-in play; the registered programmes at Southwest and St. Johns are booked through an ActiveNet account and the city does not publish their price on this page.

faqs.q: When can I actually play indoors?
faqs.a: The city lists the court count and the drop-in price for each centre and then sends you to that centre's own page for the schedule, and those pages are not covered here. Treat the four counts as what exists, not as what is free at four o'clock on a Tuesday, and check the centre before you travel.

faqs.q: What are the indoor courts made of?
faqs.a: Wood at Southwest and St. Johns: the city describes both as "Indoor wood courts" in the entry for their registered programmes, and a gym floor belongs to the building rather than to a programme. At East Portland and Montavilla the surface is not stated and is left unstated.

Not stated at any of the four. Southwest and St. Johns do say "nets provided", but only in the description of their registered programmes, not of drop-in play. Very likely the same nets go up either way, but very likely is not a source, so the field stays empty.

slots.why_this_filter: Six venues, 29 courts, and the first time this directory has been able to publish a free page at all. Every city before Portland had parks whose courts were almost certainly free to walk onto, and not one of their operators said so in writing. Portland Parks & Recreation puts the word "free" in the same line as the court count for all six of its outdoor park sites, which turns a universal assumption into a stated fact. This is not a list of courts you can probably play on for nothing; it is a list of courts the city has said so about.
slots.what_qualifies: fee_type of free, and no membership price above zero. A drop-in session with a door fee is not free, which keeps all four Portland community centres off this list at $6 and $5. The Portland Tennis Center is off it too: its pickleball runs through registration and the city publishes no figure, so its cost is not stated rather than free. Being a public park is not enough. Five other cities in this directory are full of municipal courts nobody charges for, and none of them is on a free page, because their operators never wrote it down.

faqs.q: Which Portland pickleball courts are free?
faqs.a: All six outdoor park sites: Columbia Park and Sellwood Park with eight courts each, Gabriel Park with six, Pier Park with four, Laurelhurst Park with two and Hillside Park with one. Twenty-nine courts in total, each described as free by Portland Parks & Recreation on the same line as its court count.

faqs.q: Is anything else in the city free?
faqs.a: Not that the city has said. The four community centres charge $6 for adults and $5 for seniors per drop-in session. The Portland Tennis Center states no price for its summer pickleball programme, which is not the same as being free, so it does not appear here.

faqs.q: Do I still need to bring anything?
faqs.a: A net, at four of the six. Columbia, Pier, Sellwood and Hillside all say bring your own; that is 21 of the 29 free courts. Laurelhurst and Gabriel include nets, and both are courts the city describes as 'pickleball only', so at those two a paddle and a ball are all you need.

Not stated, at every one of them. Portland Parks & Recreation says nothing about lighting anywhere on its pickleball page, so all six sites read “not stated” rather than “no”. Since the courts are open dawn to dusk rather than to a clock time, that gap matters most between October and March.

sources.evidence: Venue lines carrying count, address, indoor/outdoor and cost, e.g. "8 Outdoor hard courts, free, permanent lines, bring your own net" (Columbia Park); "4 courts, $6 for adults/$5 for seniors" (East Portland Community Center); "16 outdoor hard courts, permanent lines, nets provided. Available from mid June until early September" (Portland Tennis Center). Section headings "Outdoor courts" and "Indoor Courts". Rules: "Courts are open from Dawn to Dusk", "Limit play to one hour if others are waiting", "Be aware surface is slippery when wet". No lighting statement appears anywhere on the page.
